versions.summary_plain: A single page where you paste a recipe on one side and see the scaled ingredient list on the other. You set the servings with a stepper and flip between metric and US units; every amount updates instantly and is rounded to something you can actually measure (5 g steps, quarter cups, half spoons). Lines that aren't ingredients, like headings or 'a pinch of cinnamon', stay visible as notes. Two layout directions are shown: paste-beside-result, and paste-above-result.

screens.caption: Same recipe with the US units toggle on: cups, spoons and ounces in kitchen fractions

what_is_real: The parser is real: fractions (1 1/2, ½, 1½), ranges (2-3), bullets, and unit words are detected from free text
Scaling, metric/US conversion and kitchen rounding are real code, not mock-ups
Live update on typing, servings stepper and unit toggle all work
what_is_faked: The textarea starts with a hard-coded pancake recipe so there is something to look at
The base servings (4) is hard-coded; the real build should read 'Serves 4' from the text or let you set it
The two directions are switched by a URL parameter (?d=stack); the real build picks one
No pluralisation yet — it says '3 cup', not '3 cups'
No volume-to-weight for dry goods (cups of flour become ml, not grams); that would need an ingredient density table
versions.how_to_run: cd web && npm install && npm run dev, open http://localhost:5173 (add ?d=stack for the second direction)

scope.reason: One static page, no backend; the only real work is hardening the parser and the rounding rules with tests.

directions.title: Paste beside result
directions.idea: Two columns: your text on the left, the scaled list on the right with the controls at the top of it. Good while you are still fixing up the pasted text, because you see both at once. Cramped on narrow laptops and it collapses to one column on the phone anyway.

directions.title: Paste on top, result full width
directions.idea: The paste box is a short strip at the top, the scaled list takes the full width underneath. Treats pasting as a one-off step and gives the cooking list the most room and the largest text. You have to scroll up to edit the original.
